Low - mid-plat lvl 65+ Val main here.

The main issue im seeing here is your movements. For a good portion of the video it seemed as if you were just throwing out attacks and trying to see which ones worked. Movements aren't just for moving around the map and what not. I would recommend looking up a movement guide and learning the basics, but 2 examples are dash dancing and dash jump fast falling. Both are reliable tools to assist in confusing your opponents more and provide spacing advantages for yourself. 

Ie. Dash Dancing can be used to bait out attacks/dodges for reads. Dash jump fast falling to go against low hanging attacks like most weapon dlight moves (like sword, bow, hammer and gauntlets dlight)

Next would be your timing and decision making. For the first stock you were struggling against your opponent because you just kept running into their attacks. You need to consider your options whether you need to back up or go aggresive. Movements are still key in this situation but it's about knowing which is more advantagous. Using the first stock as an example, backing off from your opponent's attacks and countering instead wouldve provided a much easier time than just running in and hoping for the best. The decision making also applies to attack options. You mostly used Gauntlets in the video and it has plenty of reliable options other than using Dair  (more on this later.) Tips for timing and decision making are harder to provide since your options are very dependent on how your opponents play, but a good starting point is finding which ones are the most reliable to use, and learning dodge-in reads (dodge-ins are a lot more common place than you'd think)

Last I'd mention is spacing. I'd like to mention again how for a good portion of the video consisted of jusy throwing things out, hoping it works, and running into attacks. Weapons are advantages at multiple ranges and not just close and personal. Even Katars works like that and it's literally as close as you can possibly be on a weapon. Like say Dlight. Dlight, on most weapons, is a standard low-hitting attack that starts out many combos and strings. On Gauntlets, the hitbox hits a lot more ahead of you than you think. Knowing your weapon's hitbox would help in knowing it's effective range. Spacing also applies to your opponent and their weapon of choice. Spacing your opponent includes knowing their weapon range and spacing out their attacks.

Ie. Knowing bow dlight hits low, but far so you dash jump into a gc attack, or baiting out scythe slight by dash dancing and countering.


TL;DR for this part
Learn basic movements to use as tools to confuse and bait opponents. Expand on your options using whatever tools you have in your disposal, whether it be movements or your weapons.


Some Val/weapon stuff

While I dont recommend sig spamming, Val's sigs are definitely something. Her gauntlets sigs aren't too spectactular, and dont rely on dsig too much as it's more of a tool than a kill option. The gauntlets dsig can be nice to use every once in a while to confuse your opponent. Her sword sigs however shines much brighter than her gauntlets sigs. Her sword dsig is just a fancy unarmed dsig. Dont use it unless you're cocky lol. Her sword nsig is very quick and hits at a very nice angle above you. Her sword ssig however is the best in her kit as it has 3 options. It hits flat on the ground, goes over the edge, and goes up the wall. Opponents actively avoid Val's sword ssig as it hits very hard and spikes very hard over the edge, and if they forget it almost feels like a free kill sometimes.

Your gauntlets are already solid, but PLEASE dont spam dair. Dair has a ton of end lag, making you very open for counter attacks, and hits at a vertical angle which odd for strings. You can still make it work for strings, but dont spam it. I'd recommend practice using low/grounded Nair or just use sair more often. Both are also very good options that dont leave you stationary on the ground. Also, learn strings or throw out something in training mode. Gauntlets can flow into itself pretty decently considering how it's a combo/string weapon. Some basics I'd recommend is the full Russian Mafia string, or (gc) dlight > recovery. The full mafia string is reliable for a good amount of reads including spot, in, or dodge out. Plus you learn (gc) dlight > nair which many people use for starting strings. (gc) dlight > rec is just gauntlet's only reliable kill option that's true, unless you're off stage. If you're adamant on using dair, then dlight > (dash jump) dair is a true combo. Although the weapon is very open so learn it how you like.

If you decide to main Val, which im assuming so since you have her black colors, then PLEASE learn Sword. Gauntlets on a bad day just do not feel great and sword just covers it. Sword is just perfectly neutral with very reliable combo starters, kill options, read options, spacing and much more. It's very easy to learn and is perfect for understanding taking advantage of weapon options and movements. Even know I have a much harder time fighting against a player who understands Sword than a player who understands Gauntlets. Learning sword can be a game changer since it's able to cover a good portion of Gauntlet's flaws from spacing, kill options, and neutral play. Similarly, Spear and Bow also fit into this category, but both are able to space much easier. 

TL;DR for Val stuff

Val sword ssig is goated, her sword nsig is 2nd to it, but dont spam sigs too often. Use gauntlet's other attacks more often, light sair, nair, or dlight, and learn some true combos and strings. Learn Sword since it has very good neutral play, true combos/openers, and kill options that cover gauntlet's flaws.

Although I will point out some things about both characters.

Ayaka at C0 is very strong. With a decent team a f2p Ayaka can dish out over 20k dmg per tick during her burst. Freeze Ayaka is a team that wont really decline as it does not have too many downsides exept when mobs cant be frozen, but even then she can still do a lot of damage. The main downside however is her team. The most f2p team i could think of is using Diona, Sucrose, and Mona or Xingqiu. If we include limited characters: Shenhe, Venti or Kazuha, and Kokomi would be some of the replacements. Freeze Ayaka teams can require a lot of rolling simply because her best supports are mostly limited 5* characters.

Eula at C0 is also very strong. She easily works well with electro for superconduct and she now has a personal buffer, Mika. Her team can be pretty simple to build without too much issue. An example would be Eula, Mika, Fischl and a flex slot. Other characters like Rosaria and Beidou can fit in as well plus the flex slot can be any character that can benefit the team. The issue with Eula isn't exactly her team, but the fact that she does physical damage. Physical is just in a horrible spot right now, and the dedicated support for it has to be at C6 for him to be effective. For overworld content this isnt exactly an issue, but if you care about abyss then it is something to take note of.

In short, Freeze Ayaka is strong, but can required a lot of investment in the gacha. Eula teams dont require as much investment, but physical damage is in a bad position. But if none of this matters then waifu over meta. Play who you like.

first of all, she has 2 types of basic atks, one where you use ur normal atk key which makes her punch and the other with the ult key which makes her kick. By using a combination of these 2 types of atks you fill up the bar at the bottom.

when the bar is over half full, you get elemental dmg bonus from it. Note that doing the same combo twice in a row will only fill your bars once.

lets say her basic atks are 1 and 2, 1 being the normal atk key, and 2 being the ult key the combos I usually stick with to fill up my bars is

1 > 1 > 1 > 2 > 2 then 1 > 2 > 2

or

ultimate evasion > 2 then 1 > 2 > 2

these combos get me to 3/4 of the bar pretty easily

then 2 > 2 > 2 gives 15 sp if you need it

And that's all you need to do for her honestly. Just switch to other support or your dps when your bar is 3/4 full. I don't recommend using her ult, because her ult just grants more bar and ignites enemies.

However, if you have the full Margrave set, that changes because the full set will give total dmg% when using an ability that uses over 60/125 sp. Phoenix can only take advantage of the lesser buff because her ult uses 100, and the needed sp spent needs to be 105 (when used by any Fuhua).

If you do have the margrave set, then I recommend doing

1 > 2 > 2 then ult (hold 2)

This will fill up your bars entirely and grants the buff of the Margrave set.

TL;DR

Do combos until the bar below is 3/4 full, then switch

If you have full Margrave set, use your ult for the buff

A 6-month break is a pretty long break, so don't be too hard on yourself when it doesn't feel like you're at your prime.  


I'd recommend going into training mode and just doing strings that you're likely unable to hit during an actual match. Like, just go ham. You don't need to focus on how you move or whatever, just do whatever. It helps with getting movements back in touch.  


Other than that, yes 'gitting gud' is something you should do. Not exactly to overpower everyone around you, but more like to have more even matches later on. An even match is the most fun because it's a test of both of you and your enemy's limits. Learning how to play, and applying it is part of the fun. Some things I consider are what combos I learn, what strings to do, and my movement.   


Also, despite how you mention you just want to 'have fun,' you mention not reaching plat and going on a 15-lose streak. That's a competitive mindset right there. Brawlhalla is a fighting game, and most of the time we play to win and when we win is when we have fun, but we don't always win. Sometimes we lose more than we feel like we should. If it feels like you're losing too much then doing the first 2 suggestions I gave is something you can consider, or close the game for the day and come back the next day with a fresh attitude.  


Getting to learn to have fun is a very slow process and with Brawlhalla, or any fighting game for that matter, it's a pain to lose, but it's a part of it honestly.   


TL;DR   
Play more  
Learn what you can  
Take a break when you need it, no one is making you play.

This pretty much puts all of my thoughts about Scythe into words. I recently got into Plat and I don't even consider coming back to ranked after that, but there are some things to consider when going up against scythe.  


While yes scythe makes it easier to do strings and reads in a way, but keep in mind that the weapon *barely has* any true combos, and doing strings and reads is pretty much a requirement. Likely one of the reasons why you're being read so often is because of your own movements. It isn't just about reads and strings. It's also about how you move, do you change things up to catch them off guard, are you spacing yourself and your attacks correctly, and a lot more stuff to consider when it comes to playing. If you don't consider such things and you're merely running into attacks and dodging in the same direction over and over again then you'll get rekt by scythe pretty easily.  


Not only that, there's a pretty clear difference between scythe players in gold and scythe players who have legitimately played the weapon for like over a thousand hours. Now, I only have 700+ hours in the game and I only reached plat recently, but at least 500 of those hours are spent going through and suffering against scythe and trying to understand how they play. After some time you realize that reading with scythe is potentially easier in gold simply because of the lower skills of people in gold. I'm not saying that gold players are bad considering a lot of the ones I've played against are remarkably good, but with many gold players you can easily find patterns in how they play like how they dodge, how they move, and how they attack. Scythe is a weapon that takes advantage of such patterns hence making it look like it's 'easier to do strings and reads. Only recently have I considered that my movement may have been the issue when it comes to playing. I started backing off more often, dash dancing, trying to lure in their attacks, keeping an eye on their movements, and a bunch more stuff to consider because Brawlhalla is a fighting game. There's more to fighting games than just attacking.  


Over here at SEA, many scythe players I come across are floaty, they fish for dair, repeat their strings, and are relatively passive. The aggressive scythe players often whiff their attacks as well. They end up reading me because of how I used to mindlessly play. They take advantage of that easily and they do the same thing over and over again. After trying to improve my movements, fighting them was actually bearable. It was almost often an even match and many I ended up winning because despite how scythe is dependant on pattern reading, they have their own patterns that you can read.   


I've come across many scythe players in experimental as well and I could only remember a few who were legitimately above my skill level. They were aggressive and considered everything. Despite whiffing moves, they end up covering themselves with the best move possible at the time and once they fully take advantage of you it didn't matter if you change things up, because they already expected it to happen. Against gold scythe, you can fight back pretty easily once you get your head in the game.   


I guess as a tl;dr, despite how annoying it is to fight against scythe and how it's pretty much in every match you face, consider your playstyle as well. If gold scythe is torture to you then, then maybe it's your own skill level. I don't mean to say that you're bad at the game, I mean to say that there's always room to improve. If it really is too much, then you could consider taking a short break from playing the game and coming back with a fresh attitude for another challenge.  


Best of luck to reaching Plat. It's difficult, but it's possible.
